consensus_summary: The settled primary meaning is Noah’s flood as divine judgment on pervasive human sin/wickedness together with preservation of a righteous remnant, which the NT itself treats as a type of baptism and of sudden eschatological judgment; complementary alternatives include de-creation/re-creation, waters of chaos/trouble, and (secondarily) invading enemies.
book_summary: An army in motion—a nation invading, or the Lord’s own host sweeping the enemy away.
consensus_core_identification: Noahic flood (Gen 6–9) as judgment-plus-remnant-salvation with fixed NT typologies (baptism, final judgment).
book_core_identification: Invading army / nation or the Lord’s military host.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus bounds the term by the Genesis narrative and its explicit NT applications; the book bounds it by prophetic flood-of-army metaphors and omits the Noahic event entirely.
material_contradiction: The book replaces the consensus’s central referent (the Noahic judgment/salvation event and its typologies) with a distinct military-invasion metaphor; both cannot serve as the primary symbolic identification of “Flood.”
rationale: All four consensus responses converge on Noah’s flood (Gen 6–9 + 1 Pet 3, Matt 24, 2 Pet 2–3) as the primary, settled meaning, treating army-invasion imagery only as a secondary or minority alternative. The book’s sole identification is the army metaphor, supported only by the three prophetic invasion texts; this is a wholesale substitution of referent rather than a boundary adjustment or refinement of the same core, producing a DIVERGENT relation with DIFFERENT_REFERENT extension.
strongest_objection: NT texts (1 Pet 3:20–21; Matt 24:37–39; 2 Pet 3:5–7) explicitly fix the Flood as the Noahic event and its typologies, so any glossary entry that silently replaces that settled core with a secondary prophetic metaphor is incomplete.
